business_context.purpose: To provide a unified view of IT assets across AWS cloud and on-premises environments using ServiceNow ITOM Discovery.
business_drivers: Need for a single source of truth for all IT assets.
business_context.scope: ServiceNow-based Configuration Management and Discovery platform covering AWS and on-premises infrastructure.
constraints: All on-premises discovery must be performed via MID Server clusters.
Data ingestion must pass through the Identification & Reconciliation Engine (IRE).
Communication between MID Servers and ServiceNow must be outbound-only over HTTPS (Port 443).
assumptions: The ServiceNow instance is a SaaS-hosted environment with the ITOM Discovery plugin active.
Appropriate IAM roles/credentials for AWS and service accounts for on-premises targets are available.
Network connectivity exists between AWS VPCs and the on-premises environment where MID Servers are hosted if cross-environment discovery is required.
objectives: Establish automated discovery for AWS and on-premises infrastructure.

architecture_analysis.description: The architecture leverages ServiceNow MID Servers as an intermediary to perform discovery across disparate environments while maintaining a secure, outbound-only connection to the ServiceNow SaaS instance.
architecture_analysis.recommendation: Proceed with MID Server clusters for both AWS and on-prem to ensure security compliance and high availability.
alternatives: Agent-based discovery (requires software on every target).
Direct cloud-to-cloud integration without MID Servers (limited for on-prem).

scalability_and_performance.scaling_strategy: Horizontal scaling of MID Servers within clusters.

high_level_design.data_flow_overview: Discovery schedules trigger probes/patterns. ServiceNow sends tasks to the ECC Queue. MID Servers poll the ECC Queue, execute probes against targets, and return results to the ECC Queue. ServiceNow processes results via IRE and updates the CMDB.

security_architecture.authentication_mechanism: Mutual Authentication or API Key for MID Servers; SSH Keys/Service Accounts for targets; Just-in-time credential retrieval from external vaults.
security_architecture.threat_model_reference: STRIDE analysis for MID Server communication.
data_protection_measures: Integration with external credential vaults (e.g., CyberArk, HashiCorp) to avoid storing high-privilege credentials locally within the ServiceNow instance.

high_level_design.solution_overview: A ServiceNow-based ITOM Discovery solution that uses MID Server clusters to scan AWS and On-Premises environments. Data is reconciled via the IRE to maintain a clean CMDB.

integration_points.description: Communication for discovery tasks and results.

availability_and_resilience.backup_strategy: MID Server configuration files are backed up; ServiceNow instance is backed up by the provider.
availability_and_resilience.disaster_recovery_plan: Failover to secondary MID Servers in the cluster.
